# MicroDuck Live Stream Notebook Learning Line

This topic includes 7 notebooks organized by task. The video sequence is: GPU inference first, followed by RDK X5 BPU inference; each notebook has independent task labels and independent playback, and no single video will be used for different tasks.

The Notebook stores a snapshot of the executed results, making it suitable to first read the output on GitHub and then run it again in an Ubuntu/Jupyter environment as needed. During release, 64 code units were checked: all had execution counts and outputs, and no archived Python exceptions were found. This check does not mean re-executing on the reader's machine, nor does it indicate that a new training is actually initiated for each training unit.

## Notebook List

| Notebook | Main Task |
| :-- | :-- |
| `01_篮球平衡_PPO_ONNX_BPU_MuJoCo.ipynb` | Speed command, ball scene, PPO, policy export |
| `02_浏览器物理扰动_回放与接口.ipynb` | MuJoCo status, external force perturbation, web playback |
| `03_高跷行走_课程与ONNX_BPU.ipynb` | BAM, morphology course, motion smoothing, deployment contract |
| `04_摆动旋转_ONNX_BPU_MuJoCo.ipynb` | Swing task and built-in ONNX examples for the warehouse |
| `05_球平衡_FastSAC_ONNX_BPU.ipynb` | Comparison between FastSAC and another set of task interfaces |
| `06_梯面攀爬_接触与部署模板.ipynb` | Contact, landing target, course, and unfinished item boundaries |
| `07_RDK网页与多策略_BPU验收.ipynb` | Direct navigation integration, RDK TCP, multi-policy switching, BPU acceptance |

The GPU preview and historical BPU preview for each notebook can be found in [, and a summary of the demonstrations by task is provided in ](../01-task-information/selected-videos/README.md). Walking/navigation is directly connected to existing policies without training; perturbing the notebook involves physical playback and interface verification; the梯面 Notebook is currently used for contact task checks, and it cannot be claimed as stable for climbing tasks. Other notebooks provide entry points for training/continuing training of corresponding algorithms, but whether smoke training and optional training are actually running depends on the unit outputs saved in that notebook.

## Startup

```powershell
cd 02-可运行代码\microduck-playground-stilts
uv sync
uv run --with jupyter jupyter lab ..\..\03-Notebook
```

Start Jupyter on the Ubuntu workstation. Notebook will automatically search for `02-可运行代码`; if the working directory is not a specific file list, set `MICRODUCK_TOPIC_ROOT`.

## GPU and BPU Videos

Each Notebook first outputs the GPU playback for the corresponding task, followed by the previously saved BPU-in-the-loop playback. The BPU actions are generated by the X5 HBM inference, with the workstation responsible for MuJoCo physical simulation and encoding; however, the GIF in the repository is the cached result from prior runs, and does not indicate that it is running online at the board when GitHub is opened. Re-executing the BPU unit generates an MP4 and JSON report for the task in `03-Notebook/outputs/bpu_videos/` on the workstation, and overwrites the `*_bpu_latest` file for that task.

To control the size of the repository, the video output in the Notebook is changed to a GIF relative link. The original MP4 files are neither embedded in ipynb nor submitted. The GPU/BPU GIFs for the 7 tasks are all on the demo overview page; the remaining code and text result snapshots in the Notebook are retained.

## Model and BPU Injection

Notebook does not have a built-in large checkpoint. Use the policy you train or download yourself:

```powershell
$env:MICRODUCK_ONNX = "C:\models\microduck_policy.onnx"
$env:RDK_HOST = "192.168.8.128"
$env:RDK_BPU_HBM = "/home/sunrise/models/microduck_policy.hbm"
```

If you only want to check the board-side operation, you can run the verified X5 MobileNet BPU example:

```python
RDK_BPU_SMOKE_MODEL = "/opt/tros/humble/lib/dnn_benchmark_example/config/X5/mobilenetv1_224x224_nv12.bin"
RDK_BPU_SMOKE_INPUT_BYTES = 75264
```

Here, MobileNet is only used to verify that the "workstation can connect to the development board and the development board can call the BPU"; it is not part of the MicroDuck policy model. When tasks are actually executed, Notebook will select the appropriate HBM based on the task, and control the service switch between `8765` policy services through the `8766` registered on RDK, without relying on the SSH keys from Ubuntu to RDK. The above MobileNet `.bin` cannot be regarded as the task policy HBM.

The RDK control service script is `02-可运行代码/microduck-playground-stilts/scripts/rdk_bpu_policy_supervisor.py`. Only the 7 task models registered in this topic can be switched. Each time the BPU video unit is run in the Notebook, the corresponding `*_bpu_latest.mp4` and JSON report are overwritten.

## Training and Deployment Boundaries

The training of PPO/FastSAC is conducted on the workstation, and BPU is only responsible for inference. Some training units in the notebooks are controlled by environment variables, which can be skipped by default; the saved output does not necessarily reflect the actual training process. The smoke simulation training only verifies the sampling, updating, and export processes, and does not indicate that the policy has converged. `07_RDK网页与多策略_BPU验收.ipynb` is not started as required; instead, the existing walking/navigation policy is directly applied. The browser perturbation is a playback task, and no new recovery policy is trained.

The Ball Balance Notebook provides the FastSAC smoke entry point. If enabled, ONNX can be exported after a default small-scale run, and then HBM can be compiled using `hb_mapper makertbin --model-type onnx` in Ubuntu Docker. There is no need to install `hb_mapper` on X5; ordinary ONNX cannot be directly used as HBM.

The development board side requires matching the version of HBRT/BPU runtime and the corresponding task HBM. The ONNX to HBM compilation is completed using the accompanying Ubuntu Docker toolchain, and no compiler installation on the board is required. During actual re-run, it is also necessary to start the RDK service and verify that the observation dimensions, normalization, input layout, and action post-processing of HBM and ONNX are consistent.

The task video uses the RDK BPU service in the special topic and `hbm_runtime`, but does not use `CPUExecutionProvider` to generate actions. Do not directly rename ONNX to HBM; it must be compiled in practice, and the quantization, input layout, output shape, and post-processing should be checked.

## Display Policy

The GIFs saved in the Notebook are used for web pages and GitHub previews; the generated MP4/JSON files are rerun and kept in the Ubuntu `outputs/`, not committed to the repository. The physical web interaction can still run the web service in the task data directory separately.
